newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-Brazil telecoms estimates raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Brazil telecoms estimates raised.

text.p: -- Morgan Stanley & Co said it has raised its earnings estimates for Brazilian state telecommunications firms Telesp, Telerj, Telepar and Telemig as a result of last week's telecom tariff adjustments.
-- "These changes brought about a hike in average telecom rates and an end to the unattractive auto-financing system," the investment bank said in a report.
-- The bank also said it is increasing its 12-month target prices for Telesp to $360 from $300, Telerj to $205 from $170 and Telepar to $850 from $800.

-- Morgan Stanley also said it is maintaining its strong buy recommendation for Telesp, its buy ratings for Telerj and Telepar and its neutral rating for Telemig. All four are units of the federal Telebras system.
-- In the report, analyst Luiz Carvalho said the tariff adjustments will raise earnings for the firms, provide for more balanced rates and increase the momentum for the sector's privatization.
-- "The Telebras subsidiaries offer attractive valuation levels and solid earnings growth prospects," the report said.
-- The bank raised its 1997 EPS forecast for Telesp to $20.38 from $17.51, for Telerj to $9.86 from $7.58, for Telepar to $54.75 from $54.55 and for Telemig to $14.79 from $12.10.
-- It hiked its 1998 EPS estimates for Telesp to $24.46 from $21.49, for Telerj to $15.00 from $9.88, for Telepar to $70.37 from $65.77 and for Telemig to $18.16 from $14.64.

-- Morgan Stanley said its favorite local telecom stock is Telebras itself, on which it has a strong buy recommendation and a price target of $145 because it is "the most inexpensive way to play the Brazilian telecoms sector.

-- Its top pick among the subsidiaries is Telesp because it offers high pent-up demand for phone services, the most attractive concession area in Brazil, low reorganization risk and good privatization prospects, it added.
